subject: Accounting
title: Going Concern
description: Learn Going Concern in one minute.

hook.text: Every set of financial statements hides a big assumption: this company will keep operating.

buildup.text: The going concern principle assumes a business will continue into the foreseeable future.

discovery.text: It matters because a running factory is worth far more than one sold for scrap.

twist.text: When a company isn't a going concern, its asset values can plummet overnight.

climax.text: Auditors must flag any doubt about going concern—it's a red alert for investors.

punchline.text: Accounting assumes survival. If not, all bets are off.

quiz.question: What does the going concern principle assume?
options: All debts will be paid immediately

details.summary: The going concern assumption presumes that a company will continue operating indefinitely and will not liquidate in the foreseeable future. This foundational assumption underlies virtually every accounting measurement and disclosure.
details.whyItMatters: If a company isn't expected to continue operating, its assets must be valued at liquidation prices rather than historical cost—dramatically changing the entire balance sheet and the way financial statements are prepared.
takeaways: Going concern allows assets to be valued at cost rather than fire-sale liquidation prices
Auditors must evaluate whether there's substantial doubt about a company's ability to continue as a going concern
A going concern qualification in an audit report can accelerate a company's decline by triggering creditor actions

faq.question: What is the going concern assumption?
faq.answer: It's the assumption that a business will continue operating for the foreseeable future—typically at least 12 months. This allows accounting to record assets at historical cost (what they'll be worth in normal use) rather than what they'd fetch in a forced liquidation sale.

faq.question: What happens when a company is no longer a going concern?
faq.answer: When a company is expected to cease operations, financial statements switch to liquidation basis accounting. Assets are restated at estimated net realizable value (what they'd sell for), and all expected costs of winding down the business are accrued immediately.
